title: Review: Kinetic and potential energy; conservation; Work done; Work–energy theorem and dissipative forces; Force and potential energy (calculus); Gravitational potential and energy
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; E02-ap1#t2 term and clue written for the game; E01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; E02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C04-1#N.9b, E01-1#N.9a, E02-1#N.12, E02-ap1#N.2, E04-1#N.11, E05-calc-1#N.13, E01-1#N.5, E02-1#N.4a, E04-1#N.6c, E05-calc-1#N.4, E04-1#N.3, E05-calc-1#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: What an object has because it is moving; four times larger at double the speed.

items.label: Conservative force
items.clue: Type of interaction, such as gravity or an ideal spring, needed for U to exist.

items.label: Joule
items.clue: Unit equal to a 1 N force moving its point of application 1 m in its own direction.

items.label: Internal energy
items.clue: With sound, where some of a moving object's store ends up when friction or drag acts.

questions.stem: A probe is moved from a distance R to a distance 3R from the center of a planet of radius R. What fraction of the energy needed to move it from R all the way to infinity is this?
questions.explanation: To infinity: GMm/R. From R to 3R: GMm(1/R − 1/3R) = (2/3)GMm/R. Fraction 2/3.

questions.stem: A car drives at constant speed around a flat circular bend of radius 50 m. The friction force from the road on the car is 4000 N and acts towards the centre of the bend. How much work does this force do on the car while it goes a quarter of the way around?

options.text: About 3.1 × 10⁵ J, the force multiplied by the length of the arc.
About 2.0 × 10⁵ J, the force multiplied by the radius of the bend.
Zero, as the force is perpendicular to the car's velocity.
A negative amount, as friction always takes energy away from a car.

questions.explanation: θ = 90° throughout, so the work (force × displacement × cos θ) is zero. The speed, and so the kinetic energy, does not change, which agrees.

questions.stem: Three identical stones are thrown from the top of a sea cliff with the same speed: one straight up, one horizontally and one straight down. Air resistance is negligible. Which stone hits the sea with the greatest speed?

options.text: The one thrown straight down, as its velocity starts in the direction of gravity.
The one thrown upwards, as it falls back from a greater height than the others.
The one thrown horizontally, as it keeps its horizontal speed while gaining vertical speed.
All land at equal speeds: same starting kinetic energy, same drop in height.

questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy + potential energy lost = final kinetic energy, and both terms are equal for all three stones. The speeds are equal; only the directions and times of flight differ.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg ball rolls forward along the floor of a train car at 2.0 m s⁻¹ relative to the car. The train moves along a straight, level track at a constant 20 m s⁻¹ relative to the ground. What is the ball's kinetic energy as measured by an observer standing beside the track?
questions.explanation: Relative to the ground the ball moves at 20 + 2.0 = 22 m s⁻¹ (both forward). K = ½ × 0.50 × 22² = 121 J.

questions.stem: A block on a level, frictionless surface is sped up by a constant horizontal force. The work needed to speed the block up from rest to speed v is W. How many times W is needed to speed the block up from v to 3v?

The potential energy of a system is U(x) = ax² − bx³, where a and b are positive constants and x is the position of an object in the system. What is the x-component of the conservative force exerted on the object when it is at x = d?
A worker uses a rope to lower a box straight down at constant speed. Which statement about the work done on the box during the descent is correct?

options.text: The tension does positive work and gravity does negative work on the box.
The tension does negative work and gravity does positive work.
The tension and gravity both do positive work on the box as it moves.
Neither force does any work, as the box's speed does not change.

questions.stem: Object A has mass m and moves at speed 2v. Object B has mass 2m and moves at speed v. What is the kinetic energy of object A divided by the kinetic energy of object B?
questions.explanation: A: ½m(2v)² = 2mv². B: ½(2m)v² = mv². So A has twice B's kinetic energy: doubling the speed multiplies it by 4, doubling the mass only by 2.

questions.stem: A 5.0 kg box slides 4.0 m down a ramp inclined at 37° to the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the box and the ramp is 0.25. Use g = 10 m s⁻², sin 37° = 0.60 and cos 37° = 0.80. How much mechanical energy is dissipated by friction during the slide?

An ideal spring is stretched slowly from its relaxed length by an external force. Stretching it from 0 to an extension x takes work W. Stretching it further, from an extension x to an extension 2x, takes work nW. What is n?

A child on a toboggan slides across level snow. The child and toboggan have a total mass of 50 kg and slow down from 8.0 m s⁻¹ to 6.0 m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the net work done on the child–toboggan system during this time?
A car of mass m starts from rest on a level road. Its engine delivers a constant power P to the car, and friction and air resistance are negligible. What is the car's speed at time t?
